title: WIPO GRATK Treaty (2024) - Article 3: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirement
section_title: WIPO GRATK Treaty (2024) - Article 3: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirement
authority: WIPO, US FDA, European Medicines Agency (EMA), WTO
content: Article 3 of the 2024 WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge mandates that patent applicants must disclose the country of origin of genetic resources if the claimed invention is materially or directly based on genetic resources or associated traditional knowledge.

title: US FDA DSHEA (1994) & 21 CFR Part 111 - Dietary Supplement cGMP
section_title: US FDA DSHEA (1994) & 21 CFR Part 111 - Dietary Supplement cGMP
authority: WIPO, US FDA, European Medicines Agency (EMA), WTO
content: Under US FDA 21 CFR Part 111, Ayurvedic formulations exported to the USA as Dietary Supplements must undergo 100% identity testing for raw botanicals, follow batch production records, and guarantee heavy metal safety. Products cannot claim to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease and must bear the mandatory FDA structure/function disclaimer.

title: EU Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (2004/24/EC)
section_title: EU Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (2004/24/EC)
authority: WIPO, US FDA, European Medicines Agency (EMA), WTO
content: Directive 2004/24/EC provides simplified registration for traditional herbal medicinal products in the European Union. Requires evidence of 30 years of continuous traditional medicinal use, including at least 15 years within the European Community, accompanied by HMPC monograph safety data.

title: US Patent Code 35 U.S.C. 101 - Natural Products Eligibility (Myriad/Mayo Framework)
section_title: US Patent Code 35 U.S.C. 101 - Natural Products Eligibility (Myriad/Mayo Framework)
authority: WIPO, US FDA, European Medicines Agency (EMA), WTO
content: Under 35 U.S.C. 101 and the USPTO Mayo/Alice framework, naturally occurring botanical extracts, unmodified herbal molecules, or natural correlations are ineligible for patent protection in the US. To achieve patent eligibility, herbal inventions must demonstrate markedly different characteristics (structural, functional, or chemical) or an inventive application beyond the natural law.

title: European Patent Convention (EPC) Article 53(a) & 53(c)
authority: WIPO, US FDA, European Medicines Agency (EMA), WTO
content: Under Article 53(c) of the European Patent Convention, European patents shall not be granted in respect of methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body. Claims must be drafted in second medical use format (Substance X for use in the treatment of Disease Y).
